# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 58 (Bu-Vb Sk58)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Daṇḍapāṇi* Sikkhāpada is the fifty-eighth training rule in the Sekhiya chapter of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, situated within the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali as "Holding a staff", the rule forms part of the Vinaya's pedagogical deportment regulations concerning not teaching Dhamma to individuals carrying a staff [SuttaCentral].
No secondary literature passages in the supplied dossier discuss this Vinaya text; search hits for "sk 58" correspond instead to verse 58 of the *Sāṅkhyakārikā* or Tibetan accounts of the Mahāsiddhas.
According to SuttaCentral, this rule is broadly paralleled across the Vinayas of multiple early Buddhist schools [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, it corresponds directly to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Sekhiya 58, Bhikkhu Parivāra Sekhiya 58, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 58, Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Sekhiya 58, and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Parallel training rules survive in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan recensions across the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects substantial internal Pali formulaic reuse with adjacent Sekhiya rules governing teaching etiquette (notably Sekhiyas 57, 59, 60, and 61–72), as well as the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* and later Vinaya texts such as the *Vinayapiṭake Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
